query: What kinds of hardware issues appear in these incidents?

per_column.name: hardware_issue_type
per_column.rationale: This column enumerates categories/kinds of hardware issues (Printer, Monitor, Keyboard, etc.). These are TYPES/instances of the concept, not constitutive aspects OF a hardware hiccup. A faceted decomposition would carve a single hardware issue into aspects like severity, affected component, failure mode, user impact, and remediation. Instead this is a single categorical typology of the whole concept, i.e., a restatement of 'what kind of hardware issue it is' rather than a part-of aspect.

per_column.name: is_hardware_incident
per_column.rationale: A Yes/No flag for whether the incident is a hardware incident restates the identity/membership of the whole concept rather than decomposing it into constitutive aspects. It is a filter/scope indicator, not an aspect OF the hardware hiccup.

judge.rationale: Neither added column is a constitutive facet (meronym) of 'hardware_hiccups'. 'is_hardware_incident' merely flags membership in the concept, and 'hardware_issue_type' provides a single categorical typology of the whole thing. Neither carves the concept into non-overlapping aspects OF a hardware issue (e.g., affected component, failure mode, severity, user impact, resolution). They also functionally overlap: the NULLs in hardware_issue_type (418) exactly mirror the 'No' count in is_hardware_incident (418), showing the type column is essentially a refinement of the same membership signal rather than an orthogonal facet. Because the columns are restatements/scoping flags rather than parts, the facet set is empty, exhaustiveness is near zero, and mutual exclusivity is undermined by the redundancy between the two columns.
